title: Low-Cost 3D-Printed Humanoid Legs
role: Two-person team: hip and ankle joints, ROS 2 control
summary: Designing the hips and ankles of an open, 3D-printed humanoid research platform, with ROS 2 control aimed at standing and balancing.
problem: Humanoid research platforms often cost well over $10,000 (a Unitree G1 starts at $13,500), which keeps them out of reach for many university labs and student teams.
approach: We are building a modular platform from FFF 3D-printed parts that labs can print, repair and extend with common equipment. Our scope is the legs: a 2-DOF hip and a 2-DOF ankle driven by integrated joint motors with built-in drivers and encoders, carbon-fiber-filled plastic near the motors and PETG elsewhere, load cells and an IMU in each foot, and an ankle-hip balance controller in ROS 2 with Pinocchio, tested in a digital twin before it touches hardware.
result: The proposal is complete, with requirements, trade studies and component selections. Targets include under $1,200 for the hip and ankle hardware, a 200 Hz control loop and unsupported standing for more than 10 minutes.
